input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so plain `str` filenames are no longer wrapped in a tuple. A str is not an os.PathLike instance.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="foo.txt")`. The str is passed unwrapped to `edit_files`, which iterates it character by character and tries to open each character as a separate file. That breaks the most common usage. The check should be `isinstance(filename, (str, os.PathLike))`.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label. The isinstance check now tests only os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped and gets iterated character by character in edit_files. It also gives the same trigger, click.edit(filename=...) with a str filename.
